rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Printing inks, lacquers, adhesives and cleaning solvents can contain substances hazardous to health.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Workers can inhale printing vapours and mists or absorb contaminants through skin contact.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Solvents and inks can irritate skin and cause dermatitis.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Some printing products can cause skin allergy or occupational asthma.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Some solvent vapours can cause dizziness, drowsiness and effects on the central nervous system.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Long-term exposure to some ingredients can damage organs such as the liver or kidneys.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Corrosive printing chemicals can cause skin burns and eye damage.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Controls can include ventilation, enclosure, extraction, spill prevention, suitable PPE and good hand care.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: Printing-chemical risk depends on product composition, process, task, ventilation, contact route, duration and controls.

rows.source: HSE printing-solvent and ink exposure control
rows.verified: HSE printing evidence is product-, process-, task-, worker-, workplace- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Cholera is caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae serogroups O1 or O139.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Transmission is associated with contaminated food or water.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Illness can include profuse watery diarrhoea, vomiting and severe dehydration.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Cholera occurs mainly in parts of Asia, Africa and the Americas and UK cases are generally travel associated.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Untreated water and poorly cooked food, particularly seafood, can increase risk in affected areas.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Cholera vaccination is recommended only for some travellers.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Personal hygiene and food-and-water precautions reduce travel-related cholera risk.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Suspected cholera is notifiable and diagnostic samples should include relevant clinical and travel history.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: Cholera risk depends on destination, outbreak activity, food and water exposure, hygiene, vaccination and traveller factors.

rows.source: UKHSA cholera public-health guidance
rows.verified: UKHSA cholera evidence is destination-, exposure-, traveller-, laboratory-, patient- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
